newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: MARCO POLO TO REDEVELOP SITE IN 1999.
newsitem.headline: MARCO POLO TO REDEVELOP SITE IN 1999.

text.p: Marco Polo Developments said on Monday it has decided to redevelop the site on which The Marco Polo Singapore hotel stands into a residential condominium development in 1999.
Marco Polo, which is a unit of Hong Kong's New Asia Realty & Trust Co, said in a statement the redevelopment would consist of 150 apartment units and eight penthouses.
The company said it planned to launch sales of the project in the first half of 1998. It would discontinue the operations of the hotel by January 1999 and undertake the redevelopment immediately.
Marco Polo said it arrived at this decision after taking into account that the hotel is situated on a prime freehold site comparable to that of the new Ardmore Park being developed by the group.
Some 322 Units in the Ardmore Park project have been sold at an average of Singapore $1,862 per sq ft resulting in a total value of S$1.7 billion for the group.

Assuming the units in the Marco Polo site are sold at the same average price achieved at Ardmore Park, total sales from the redevelopment of the hotel site were estimated to be in the region of S$760 million, it said.

Marco Polo said it had been given permission to redevelop the site and had paid a development charge of S$1.92 million and a S$1.21 million differential premium for a small strip of land for the redevelopment.
The company said profits from the project were expected to be recognised over four to five years from 1999/2000 onwards.
